questions.stem: Find out the wrong statement about Levator Ani muscle function and support:

options.label: C
options.text: Its Parts are iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus

questions.solutionHtml:
Attached to pelvic brim
  • Levator Ani Muscle is not attached to the pelvic brim. It takes its origin from the body of the pubis, the arcus tendinous of the levator ani (a thickened part of the obturator fascia), and the ischial spine.
  • Levator Ani Muscles Innervated by the anterior ramus of S4 and branches of the pudendal nerve (roots S2, S3 and S4).
  • The levator ani is a broad sheet of muscle. It is composed of three separate paired muscles; pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus.

Pelvic Diaphragm




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1245.

questions.stem: Correct sequence of structure in spermatogenesis event:SpermatozoaSpermatogoniaSpermatocytesSpermatidSelect the correct answer using the code below:
questions.solutionHtml:
2 → 3 → 4 → 1
  • Spermatogenesis is the process by which haploid spermatozoa develop from germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testis. This process starts with the mitotic division of the stem cells located close to the basement membrane of the tubules. 
  • The spermatogonium undergoes mitotic division to form two primary spermatocytes (largest germ cells). The primary spermatocytes undergo first meiotic division (reduction division) to form two secondary spermatocytes. The secondary spermatocytes thus have a haploid number of chromosomes.
  • Each secondary spermatocyte immediately undergoes second meiotic division (i.e., mitotic division) to form two spermatids, each with haploid number of chromosomes.
  • Each spermatid gradually changes its stage to become spermatozoa or sperm. This transformation of circular spermatid into an elongated spermatozoon is called spermiogenesis.
  • Thus from one primary spermatocyte four spermatozoa are formed; two with 22 autosomes and one X chromosome (22 + X, 22 + X) and two with 22 autosomes and one Y chromosome (22 + Y, 22 + Y).


Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 17,18.

questions.stem: All of the following are branches of External carotid artery (ECA) supplying the nasal septum except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Anterior Ethmoidal Artery

Blood supply of Nasal septum

  • The anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteriesarise from the ophthalmic artery in the medial third of the orbit. Ophthalmic artery is a branch of internal carotid artery.
  • Superior labial artery is a branch of the facial artery. (Facial artery is a branch of the external carotid artery).
  • Sphenopalatine artery & Greater palatine artery is a branch of maxillary artery. (Maxillary artery is a branch of external carotid artery)



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-547.

ANSA CERVICALIS

questions.stemHtml: In the following image, the person started surface marking of thorax from 3rd costal cartilage to 6th costal cartilage and a marking point was given. The marked points identifies-
questions.solutionHtml:
Right atrium
  • The region marked corresponds to the surface marking for the right atrium.
  • The costal margin, xiphoid process, and the mid-clavicular line are seen in this image.
  • The examiner draws a laterally convex line that extends from a level below the 2nd costal cartilage (as clued in by the sternal angle) i.e., 3rd costal cartilage to about 3 spaces below - i.e., the 6th costal cartilage.
  • This line is about 1.2 cm lateral to the sternal edge. These suggest that the region marked corresponds to the surface marking for the right atrium.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No-288,289.

questions.stemHtml: Action of the muscle attached to the marked area?
questions.solutionHtml:
Abduction
  • The image shows the greater trochanter and the muscle fibers of the gluteus medius and gluteus minimus attach here and their function is to abduct and rotate the thigh medially.
  • Both are innervated by the superior gluteal nerve (L4, L5, S1)

Attachment of femur bone




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No-78,79.

questions.stem: Structure that divides liver anatomically based on Couinaud’ s classification system is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Portal veins
  • The structure that divides the liver in Couinaud’s classification system is the portal vein.
  • The Couinaud classification of liver anatomy divides the liver into eight functionally independent segments. Each segment has its own vascular inflow, outflow and biliary drainage.
  • In the centre of each segment there is a branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct.

Functional liver segment




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No-359,360.

questions.stem: Which of the following finger is having two dorsal interossei muscle:
questions.solutionHtml:
Middle finger

The Middle Finger has two dorsal interossei.

  • The four dorsal interossei muscles are bipennate in nature
  • First two attach to radial side of proximal phalanx of index and middle finger & blend with dorsal digital expansion
  • The third & fourth to ulnar side of the proximal phalanx of middle and ring finger & blend with dorsal digital expansion.
  • Second and third are attached to the radial & ulnar sides of the middle finger.

Dorsal Interossei causes Abduction of fingers from the Middle/3rd finger.




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No-129-131.
